payload.summary: Discovery: src/greeting.mjs exports only greet(name) whose body is a single inline template literal `Hello, ${name}!` — that literal is the greeting-string construction to extract into new internal src/format.mjs. No src/format.mjs exists yet; src/ contains only greeting.mjs. Two required validators are configured in .harness/project.yaml (validation.commands id=fixture-greeting → `node scripts/validate.mjs`; validation.validators id=contract-test → `node scripts/contract.mjs`) and both import greet from ../src/greeting.mjs. The critical constraint is contract.mjs, which fails with "unexpected public export" if src/greeting.mjs exports any key outside ["greet","FAREWELL"], so format.mjs must be imported (e.g. ./format.mjs) but never re-exported; both validators assert greet("AEH") === "Hello, AEH!". Only other references to greet are the two validators — no test/ directory, no other importers, no package.json exports map. openspec/config.yaml explicitly directs pure no-behavior refactors to declare skip_specs: true instead of authoring spec deltas.

relevantFiles.reason: Source of the refactor: sole public entry; greet body holds the inline greeting-string construction to be extracted; must keep exporting exactly greet with unchanged behavior.

Configured required validator fixture-greeting (`npm test`); asserts greet is a function and greet("AEH") === "Hello, AEH!".
Configured required validator contract-test; enforces the export surface of src/greeting.mjs (keys must be subset of ["greet","FAREWELL"]) plus behavior — the tightest constraint on this refactor.

test script → node scripts/validate.mjs; no exports map, so no subpath-export impact for the new internal module.

payload.summary: Discovery: src/greeting.mjs exports only greet(name) whose body is a single inline template literal `Hello, ${name}!` — that literal is the greeting-string construction to extract into new internal src/format.mjs. No src/format.mjs exists yet; src/ contains only greeting.mjs. Two required validators are configured in .harness/project.yaml (validation.commands id=fixture-greeting → `node scripts/validate.mjs`; validation.validators id=contract-test → `node scripts/contract.mjs`) and both import greet from ../src/greeting.mjs. The critical constraint is contract.mjs, which fails with "unexpected public export" if src/greeting.mjs exports any key outside ["greet","FAREWELL"], so format.mjs must be imported (e.g. ./format.mjs) but never re-exported; both validators assert greet("AEH") === "Hello, AEH!". Only other references to greet are the two validators — no test/ directory, no other importers, no package.json exports map. openspec/config.yaml explicitly directs pure no-behavior refactors to declare skip_specs: true instead of authoring spec deltas.

relevantFiles.reason: Source of the refactor: sole public entry; greet body holds the inline greeting-string construction to be extracted; must keep exporting exactly greet with unchanged behavior.

Target of the extraction — does not exist yet (glob src/**/* returns only src/greeting.mjs); new internal module that must hold the greeting-string construction and must not be re-exported from greeting.mjs.
Configured required validator fixture-greeting (`npm test`); asserts greet is a function and greet("AEH") === "Hello, AEH!".
Configured required validator contract-test; enforces the export surface of src/greeting.mjs (keys must be subset of ["greet","FAREWELL"]) plus behavior — the tightest constraint on this refactor.
Declares both configured validators (fixture-greeting command and contract-test adapter, both required, 60s timeout) that must remain unchanged.
test script → node scripts/validate.mjs; no exports map, so no subpath-export impact for the new internal module.
Policy: pure no-behavior refactor should use skip_specs: true rather than authored spec deltas.

evidence: src/greeting.mjs:1-3 → `export function greet(name) { return `Hello, ${name}!`; }` — the template literal is the entire greeting-string construction
glob src/**/* → only src/greeting.mjs (no existing format.mjs)
findings.notes: Extraction is a pure move of the template literal into a format.mjs helper imported by greeting.mjs.

evidence: .harness/project.yaml:271-275 → commands: - id: fixture-greeting, command: node scripts/validate.mjs, required: true
.harness/project.yaml:276-281 → validators: - id: contract-test, adapter: contract-test, command: node scripts/contract.mjs, required: true
package.json:6 → "test": "node scripts/validate.mjs"
scripts/validate.mjs:1,4 → imports greet; asserts typeof greet === "function" && greet("AEH") === "Hello, AEH!"
scripts/contract.mjs:1,4-7 → imports greet, asserts behavior, then dynamically imports ../src/greeting.mjs and rejects keys outside ["greet","FAREWELL"]
findings.notes: Both validators are configured and required; neither may be modified.

evidence: scripts/contract.mjs:7 → `if (Object.keys(moduleValue).some((key) => !["greet", "FAREWELL"].includes(key))) failures.push("unexpected public export")`
src/greeting.mjs currently exports exactly greet (single export statement at line 1)
findings.notes: Re-exporting format helpers from greeting.mjs would fail contract-test; format.mjs must be imported, not re-exported. Note allow-list also tolerates FAREWELL, but greeting.mjs does not currently export it — do not add it.

evidence: grep for greet|greeting|FAREWELL matches only: src/greeting.mjs:1, scripts/validate.mjs:1,4, scripts/contract.mjs:1,4,5,6,7, and .harness/project.yaml:272 (validator id fixture-greeting)
glob **/*.{mjs,js,json,yaml,yml,md} → 7 files; no test/ directory, no other importers
findings.notes: No other call sites or fixtures depend on greeting internals.

evidence: openspec/config.yaml:7 → "For pure refactors/tooling/docs/internal-readability changes with no observable behavior delta, declare `skip_specs: true`"
openspec/config.yaml:18 → "Do not create a spec delta for a pure no-behavior refactor; use the OpenSpec skip_specs marker instead."
findings.notes: This change is a pure internal refactor with no observable behavior delta, so spec authoring should use the skip_specs marker.

moduleBoundaries: src/greeting.mjs — public entry module; sole public export greet; imports internal src/format.mjs
src/format.mjs — new internal-only module; not part of the public export surface, never re-exported
scripts/validate.mjs + scripts/contract.mjs — required validators consuming the public surface; read-only for this change
.harness/project.yaml validation block — configuration source for both validators; read-only for this change
tests: node scripts/validate.mjs (configured command id=fixture-greeting, required; also `npm test`)
node scripts/contract.mjs (configured validator id=contract-test, adapter contract-test, required)
No dedicated test/ directory exists; these two scripts are the complete executable acceptance evidence.
dependencies: Node.js ESM via .mjs extension (package.json has no "type" field and no "exports" map — no external dependencies declared)
Validators depend on ../src/greeting.mjs path and on the exact output string "Hello, AEH!"
risks: Export-surface regression: any re-export (e.g. `export { formatGreeting }`) added to src/greeting.mjs fails contract-test's `unexpected public export` check (scripts/contract.mjs:7).
Behavior drift: the extracted construction must produce byte-identical output, since both validators assert greet("AEH") === "Hello, AEH!" (scripts/validate.mjs:4, scripts/contract.mjs:5).
Module resolution: new file must use the .mjs extension and a relative ./format.mjs import; no bundler/exports-map is present to mask a wrong path.
Scope creep risk: adding FAREWELL (allowed by contract.mjs allow-list) or touching validator files would violate the frozen instruction to keep both configured validators unchanged.
Spec overhead: openspec/config.yaml requires skip_specs: true for pure no-behavior refactors — authoring behavioral deltas would contradict repo policy.
openQuestions: Exact internal helper name/signature for src/format.mjs (e.g. formatGreeting(name)) is unspecified — planner/spec decision, not observable.
Whether greeting.mjs should keep its function body delegating (`return formatGreeting(name)`) or inline the import call — implementation detail with no behavioral difference.
